newsitem.title: USA: Raines says White House considering CPI panel.
newsitem.headline: Raines says White House considering CPI panel.

text.p: The White House is considering a proposal to set up an independent panel that would determine cost of living adjustments for federal benefit programs but no decision has been made yet, budget chief Franklin Raines said Wednesday.

The idea of such a panel was suggested recently by Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, Republican of Mississippi. It has also been advocated by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, amid a widespread belief among economists that the Consumer Price Index, which is now used to index federal programs, overstates inflation.
Recently, press reports have suggested the White House may be moving closer to the idea.
However, Raines said, "We've made absolutely no decision about the benefits or lack of benefits of such a panel."
"We have a suggestion from Senator Lott and Senator (Democratic Leader Tom) Daschle," Raines said. "We're pursuing that in discussions in professional quarters and on the Hill."
Although one press report indicated that the White House may announce a decision regarding the CPI on Friday, Raines said there was no deadline.
He said the issue would be pursued by the administration over the next days and weeks.
